rules.title: Oversized HTTP Cookie Values Possible C2 Channel
rules.description: Detects HTTP sessions where Cookie or Set-Cookie values are unusually long or high-entropy. Okrum has hidden actual C2 messages in Cookie and Set-Cookie headers (T1001).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Wide-Structure Beacons to Versioned API Path with Binary Body
rules.description: Detects HTTP POST beacons to a versioned API path that carry an octet-stream body, the stable structure left behind when an implant pads check-ins with junk data. Sigma cannot compute variance, so this rule matches structure and the paired SPL query adds the size-spread check.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Rundll32 Starting a File From Temp or Downloads (TH-01)
rules.description: Detects rundll32.exe starting a module from a user-writable folder such as Temp or Downloads. Attackers that hide a stage inside an image file often drop the extracted file next to the picture and start it with rundll32. This rule is a workflow cue, not proof of steganography: correlate the same host with a recent image download before escalating.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Library-Path Fetch from Non-CDN Host (T1001.003)
rules.description: Detects HTTP GET requests for jQuery-style library paths where the destination host is not an approved CDN. Attackers hide C2 tasking inside library-shaped fetches.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Possible USB Cellular Modem or RNDIS Network Adapter Attached
rules.description: Detects the load of RNDIS or USB NCM network drivers. These drivers appear when a phone tether or a USB cellular modem is attached. Attackers use such adapters to send data over a cellular link that bypasses corporate egress monitoring. This rule covers threat 1 of the T1011 ranking.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Bluetooth Transfer Tools Started by an Unexpected Parent
rules.description: Detects the start of the Windows Bluetooth file transfer wizard (fsquirt.exe) or the Bluetooth settings panel (bthpropscpl.exe) when the parent process is not the usual user shell. Attackers drive these tools from scripts to push staged files over OBEX, the Object Exchange Bluetooth file-push profile. This rule covers threat 1 of the T1011.001 ranking.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Scheduled Task Creation Referencing Archiver or Sync Tooling
rules.description: Detects a Windows scheduled task being created (Event ID 4698) whose action line references archivers, downloaders, or sync/upload utilities. This is the persistence-and-staging signature of automated exfiltration (T1020). Review the creator account and the task trigger time.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Cloud Traffic Mirror Session Created or Modified
rules.description: Detects creation, modification, or deletion of traffic mirror resources in AWS CloudTrail. An attacker with a cloud network role can copy whole subnets to a mirror target they control with one API call. Azure vTap and GCP packetMirroring (packetMirrors.insert) are the equivalents - apply the same logic to those providers' audit logs. Maps to ATT&CK analytic AN1131 (mirror policy changes to unapproved destinations).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Admin Share Access Followed by Remote Process Creation
rules.description: Correlates an ADMIN$ share access (Event 5145) with a process creation (4688) or service install (7045) on the same host within 10 minutes. This shows the classic copy-then-execute lateral movement step over SMB. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Internal Remote Service Port Sweep from One Host
rules.description: Detects one internal host connecting to 20 or more different hosts on remote-service ports (SSH 22, SMB 445, RDP 3389, WinRM 5985) within 10 minutes. This is the recon step attackers run before choosing a service to move with, and it is also how ransomware worms find their next target. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Remote Interactive and Network Logon from Same Unusual Source
rules.description: Detects the same source IP producing both a remote interactive logon (Type 10, RDP-style) and a network logon (Type 3, SMB/WinRM-style) on the same host within 30 minutes. This service-hopping pattern marks attackers mixing tools, not normal users. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Single Source Logons to Multiple Hosts via Remote Services
rules.description: Detects one source IP creating successful logons (network Type 3 or remote interactive Type 10) on 3 or more different hosts within 10 minutes. This fan-out shape fits lateral movement with SMB, WinRM, and RDP, or a worm - it does not fit normal administration from a workstation. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: SSH Accepted Public Key from Unusual Source Host
rules.description: Detects a successful SSH login using a public key from a source that is not an approved bastion or admin host. Attackers with a stolen private key need no password, so this line is often the single footprint of the pivot.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Suspicious Remote Service Installation
rules.description: Detects a service installation with a PsExec-style name or a binary path inside an admin share. Attackers copy a small service program into ADMIN$ and start it remotely to run commands as SYSTEM on the target host.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: WinRM Remote Execution with Encoded PowerShell
rules.description: Detects PowerShell script blocks or process creations that use encoded commands (-enc / -EncodedCommand / FromBase64String). Delivered through WinRM, this combination is a strong sign of attacker remote execution.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: RDP Enabled via Registry Modification
rules.description: Detects a registry change that turns RDP on (fDenyTSConnections set to 0) or weakens RDP security settings. Malware and hands-on attackers enable RDP to keep a simple way back into a machine.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: RDP Fan-Out to Multiple Hosts from One Source
rules.description: Detects one source IP creating RDP sessions on 5 or more different hosts within 24 hours. This shape fits attackers sweeping the network and rare worm behavior, not normal admin work. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: RDP Logon from Unusual Source Host
rules.description: Detects an interactive RDP logon (Logon Type 10) from a source IP that is not an approved jump server. Attackers use RDP to move between Windows machines after stealing valid credentials.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: RDP Password Guessing Burst
rules.description: Detects 10 or more failed RDP logons (Logon Type 10) from the same source IP within 10 minutes. This pattern shows password guessing or password spraying against exposed or internal RDP. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(IpAddress) >= 10 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: RDP Session Hijack with Tscon
rules.description: Detects tscon.exe called with a /dest: parameter. Attackers with SYSTEM rights use this to redirect another user's active RDP session to their own screen, taking over the session without knowing the password.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: RDP Successful Logon After Failed Attempts from Same Source
rules.description: Correlates failed RDP logons (4625) with a successful RDP logon (4624, Type 10) from the same source IP within 30 minutes. This shows a password guess that worked and must be treated as a possible incident. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: RDP Tunneling Tool Executed
rules.description: Detects the launch of well-known tunneling tools or any process in a Temp folder using reverse port forwarding. Attackers use these to reach internal RDP through an allowed outbound port.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Security Log Cleared After RDP Activity
rules.description: Detects a cleared Security log (Event 1102). Attackers often clear logs after RDP sessions to hide lateral movement. Correlate this event with the Type 10 logons that came before it on the same host.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Admin Type 3 Logon from Non-Jump Host
rules.description: Detects a network (Type 3) logon by an admin-like account from a host outside the jump server range. Pairs with 5145 admin share access in the SIEM version of this rule.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Executable or Script Written to ADMIN$ Share
rules.description: Detects executable files written into the hidden ADMIN$ share. Attackers stage tools there before running them with a remote service.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Impacket-Style Service Names and Command Patterns
rules.description: Detects known impacket executor service names in 7045 and the cmd.exe quiet-mode patterns those tools type into 4688.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: PsExec-Style Remote Service Install
rules.description: Detects the default service name of PsExec and short random service names that remote execution tools create over admin shares.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Remote Command Execution via WMI Node or Admin Share Path
rules.description: Detects command lines that target remote systems with WMI (/node:) or that reference the hidden ADMIN$ share directly.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Sensitive Share Access by Unusual User
rules.description: Detects file access (5145) to HR or Finance shares by accounts that are not on the known service account allowlist.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Share Enumeration Burst from a Single Source
rules.description: Detects one source connecting to the IPC$ share on many hosts within 10 minutes. Tools do this to map which servers expose shares. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Admin Share Access Following Network Logon from Same Host
rules.description: Detects a read of the C$ or ADMIN$ admin share that follows a Type 3 network logon from the same source host within 10 minutes. After DCOM execution, attackers fetch command output or copy tools this way. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: DCOM Activation Permission Error (Event 10036)
rules.description: Detects rejected COM activations in the Microsoft-Windows-DCOM Operational log. The message contains the client address. Repeated errors from a host that does not administer the target suggest DCOM probing or lateral movement attempts with wrong permissions.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: DCOM Lateral Movement via MMC20.Application (PowerShell 4104)
rules.description: Detects PowerShell script blocks that create the MMC20.Application COM object on a remote computer and call ExecuteShellCommand. This is the classic DCOM lateral movement pattern published by enigma0x3 in 2017.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: DCOM Lateral Movement via ShellWindows or ShellBrowserWindow (PowerShell 4104)
rules.description: Detects PowerShell script blocks that create hidden Explorer COM objects (ShellWindows or ShellBrowserWindow) and call ShellExecute, or that resolve any Shell-named ProgID together with CreateInstance; the DCOM remote execution pattern.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: DistributedCOM Permission Settings Events 10016 (Hygiene Baseline)
rules.description: Counts DistributedCOM event 10016 records in the System log. These events fire on almost every default Windows host, so this rule is not an alert. Use it to build the inventory of hosts with wide COM permission settings and to find machines that missed the 2022 DCOM hardening.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Encoded PowerShell Spawned by explorer.exe (Possible DCOM ShellExecute)
rules.description: Detects PowerShell started with an encoded command by explorer.exe. The ShellWindows and ShellBrowserWindow DCOM objects use a hidden Explorer window to ShellExecute programs on the target, so a server showing this pair means a remote activation just ran.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: RPC Endpoint Mapper Sweep to Multiple Hosts
rules.description: Detects a single host connecting to TCP 135 on more than 10 different destinations within 10 minutes. This is RPC/DCOM reconnaissance before lateral movement, not normal administration from a management zone. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Sensitive Access to lsass.exe Memory (Sysmon 10)
rules.description: Detects a process requesting access to lsass.exe with rights that allow reading memory. After a DCOM pivot, attackers dump credential material this way to reach the next hop, often with comsvcs.dll MiniDump.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Shell Spawned by MMC (Possible DCOM ExecuteShellCommand)
rules.description: Detects cmd, powershell, or wscript processes created by mmc.exe. MMC is a graphical console; it does not spawn shells on its own. A remote DCOM ExecuteShellCommand call through MMC20.Application does exactly this.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Direct Root SSH Login Accepted
rules.description: Detects any successful SSH login as root with a key or a password. Hardened baselines set PermitRootLogin no, so every hit is a configuration break or an attacker with direct root access.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: New Key Added to authorized_keys
rules.description: Detects a write to an authorized_keys file that was not made by an approved CI/CD or configuration management account. Attackers add their own public key for persistence (T1098.004) after stealing a first set of credentials.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: One Source Logs Into Many Hosts with Public Keys
rules.description: Detects one source IP and account accepting public key logins on 3 or more distinct destination hosts within 24 hours. This fan-out pattern matches a stolen deploy or admin key used to walk the estate. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Script Execution from Temp Path inside an SSH Session
rules.description: Detects a shell started by sshd that runs a script from /tmp or /dev/shm. This is the staging pattern of ransomware and coin-miner crews that arrive over SSH and execute their payload from a hidden temp folder.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: SSH Client Started with Agent Forwarding
rules.description: Detects an ssh process started with the -A (agent forwarding) flag, seen in auditd execve records. Attackers use this flag to reach the next hop with an agent socket that is not theirs, so each hit on a server should be checked.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: SSH Password Brute Force Burst
rules.description: Detects 10 or more failed SSH password logons from the same source IP within 10 minutes. This pattern shows password guessing or spraying against exposed or weak-password servers. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) >= 10 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: SSH Public Key Login from Unusual Source Subnet
rules.description: Detects a successful SSH login with a public key whose source IP is not an approved bastion or admin subnet. Stolen keys are usually used from workstations, build servers, or cloud hosts that the account never used.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: SSH Tunnel or Port Forward Started from a Server
rules.description: Detects an ssh process with dynamic (-D), remote (-R), local (-L), or tun-interface (-w) forwarding flags. Triage hits on servers first; admins normally run -L only from laptops.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: sshd_config Modified
rules.description: Detects a write to /etc/ssh/sshd_config using the auditd watch with key sshd-config-watch. Changes can enable root login, password login, or weak algorithms, which makes every other SSH attack cheaper.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Inbound VNC Port from Unusual Source
rules.description: Detects an inbound network connection to VNC ports 5900-5906 whose source is not an approved support network. Internet-exposed VNC servers with weak legacy passwords are a common retail and kiosk foothold.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Large Egress After VNC Session
rules.description: Detects a VNC session on port 5900 that moves an unusually large volume of bytes. Remote-control visits that carry a gigabyte are usually setup for collecting and copying data out of stores, kiosks, and file servers. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: New VNC Service Installed
rules.description: Detects the installation of a new Windows service with a VNC-related name. Attackers install VNC as a service for persistent full-desktop access on servers and point-of-sale terminals.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Security Service Stopped After Remote VNC Session
rules.description: Detects a security or antivirus service entering the stopped state. Correlate with an inbound or active session on port 5900 within the timeframe: an attacker controlling the desktop through VNC is the usual reason protection turns off without a change ticket.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: VNC Password Brute Force Indicators
rules.description: Detects 20 or more connections to VNC port 5900 from one source within 10 minutes. Classic VNC authentication has no lockout, so password guessers reconnect in a tight loop and the firewall is the only witness. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) >= 20 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: VNC Persistence via Registry Run Key
rules.description: Detects a write to a Windows Run autorun key whose stored value references VNC. Rogue VNC servers use Run keys to restart at every login without needing a service or admin rights.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: VNC Server Process from User-Writable Path
rules.description: Detects a VNC-named executable running from a folder users can write to. Attackers drop small VNC servers into Public, Temp, or AppData folders for hidden remote-control access that survives reboots.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Account Created During WinRM Session
rules.description: Detects a user account creation (event 4720) on a host that had a WinRM network logon (event 4624, Type 3, Negotiate) moments earlier. The near operator ties the two events together within the timeframe on the same machine. Attackers create accounts this way to keep access even after the stolen password is reset. On a domain controller the new account is a domain account; on member servers it is a local one. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Encoded PowerShell Command via WinRM
rules.description: Detects PowerShell script blocks that carry an encoded command, seen in event 4104 or on the command line in event 4688. Attackers encode payloads with -EncodedCommand or FromBase64String to hide them from plain-text rules. The 4104 event records the decoded content, so the rule leads straight to the payload.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Invoke-Command Fan-Out from Unusual Host
rules.description: Detects PowerShell script blocks that call Invoke-Command with a list of -ComputerName targets from a host that is not an approved jump server. This is one command prepared to hit many servers at once. Hosts outside the approved jump server list are the interesting ones.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: LSASS Memory Dump via comsvcs.dll
rules.description: Detects rundll32 loading comsvcs.dll with the MiniDump export against lsass.exe, or a process opening lsass with read access (Sysmon event 10, GrantedAccess 0x1010). Attackers favor this pair because rundll32 is signed and no dump tool ever lands on disk. Correlate with the WinRM session that carried the command.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Mass WinRM Network Connections from One Source
rules.description: Detects one machine opening WinRM connections (TCP 5985 or 5986) to five or more different targets within ten minutes. This is the network shape of an Invoke-Command sweep across many servers. Check the source against the admin tier before you judge it, because patching tools also fan out. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: WinRM Listener or Service Configuration Change
rules.description: Detects writes to WinRM listener registry keys and changes to the WinRM service configuration key. Attackers enable or modify listeners to keep a remote channel open, or install a service named after WinRM. Pair this rule with event 7045 (new service installed) filtered on WinRM, which the matching SPL query includes.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: WinRM Remote PowerShell Session on Non-Jump Host
rules.description: Detects wsmprovhost.exe, the process that hosts remote PowerShell commands, starting on a machine that is not an approved jump server. The rule also matches its children, because every remote command runs inside it. One hit outside the admin tier is the strongest single sign of WinRM lateral movement.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: AWS CloudTrail Logging Stopped or Trail Deleted
rules.description: Detects attempts to stop or delete CloudTrail logging, including denied attempts blocked by a service control policy. A denied attempt still proves a hostile actor is active inside the account.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: AWS Console Login Without MFA or from New Country
rules.description: Detects successful console logins where MFA was not used (typical for a replayed stolen session cookie) or the login comes from a country outside the expected list. Covers the LAPSUS$ and Scattered Spider access pattern.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: AWS SSM SendCommand by Unusual Principal
rules.description: Detects the SendCommand API call made by a principal that is not one of the approved automation roles. Attackers with stolen credentials use SendCommand to run shell commands on virtual machines without any SSH or console login.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: AWS SSM StartSession from Unusual Principal
rules.description: Detects SSM Session Manager start events by principals outside the approved bastion and on-call list. A stolen cloud identity can open an interactive shell on private VMs with no SSH key and no network path to the VM.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Bulk S3 Object Read by Unusual Principal
rules.description: Detects 1000 or more S3 GetObject events by one principal within 30 minutes, excluding known backup roles. Matches the bulk exfiltration pattern of the 2024 stolen-credential data theft campaigns. Requires S3 data events. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(userIdentity.arn) >= 1000 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: New IAM Access Key Created and Used Within One Hour
rules.description: Correlates an IAM CreateAccessKey event with follow-up API activity by the same principal within one hour. Shows a freshly minted key that is already being used - the persistence step seen in cloud intrusion campaigns. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Rare Cloud API Enumeration Burst by One Principal
rules.description: Detects a single principal calling 50 or more distinct Describe*, List*, or Get* event names within 15 minutes. Shows programmatic enumeration of the account, which usually precedes execution or exfiltration steps. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: AWS EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint Created
rules.description: Detects the creation of an EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint. This API is a direct change to the private network path of a VPC and is rare in most accounts. Attackers who hold a valid IAM role use it to reach private VMs without a public IP or VPN.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: AWS EC2 Serial Console SSH Public Key Sent
rules.description: Detects a key push for the EC2 Serial Console. The serial console is a root-level recovery door that works even when networking is broken, so any use deserves a page to a human.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Instance Connect Endpoint Deleted and Recreated Within 24h
rules.description: Aggregation rule: the same principal or account deletes an Instance Connect Endpoint and creates a new one within 24 hours. Attackers rotate endpoints to escape temporary reach or to mimic cleanup. Approved pipelines do this on schedule, so group by identity and compare against the change calendar.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Reverse SSH Tunnel Process After Instance Connect Session
rules.description: Detects an ssh process started with a reverse tunnel flag (-R) on a Linux instance, which is a common way for attackers to call home after gaining a shell through Instance Connect. For environments without endpoint telemetry, watch netflow for long-lived high-byte outbound sessions right after a SendSSHPublicKey event.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: SendSSHPublicKey by Machine Identity Without Recent ConsoleLogin
rules.description: Detects a temporary SSH key push by a machine identity (userIdentity.type AssumedRole, the identity a program or role session uses). Humans normally log in to the console first; robot roles should not behave like people. The classic rule below matches the machine-identity part. The Splunk search adds the true 24-hour ConsoleLogin lookback with a subsearch.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: SendSSHPublicKey by Unusual Principal
rules.description: Detects a temporary SSH key being pushed to an EC2 instance by a principal that is not on the approved admin or pipeline allow list. A leaked CI/CD role calling this API is a strong sign of direct cloud VM access abuse.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: SSH Login Marked ec2-instance-connect with Unknown Key Fingerprint
rules.description: Detects an accepted SSH login on a Linux instance whose auth log message contains the provider marker ec2-instance-connect, where the key fingerprint is not one of the approved admin fingerprints. This is where the cloud event becomes a real session on the machine.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Archiver or Splitter Started with Volume-Split Flags
rules.description: Detects archivers or file splitters started with volume flags such as -v9m, -v5m, or split -b. Creating fixed-size parts is the preparation step of T1030 chunked exfiltration, and the part files are high-value disk artifacts.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Long-Lived Outbound TLS Session with Bulk Client Payload
rules.description: Detects an outbound Zeek connection where one session carries 10 MB or more of client payload and stays open for 300 seconds or longer. Long-lived, upload-heavy sessions to a single peer are the transport shape of exfiltration over a C2 channel (T1041). Pair with the Splunk SPL for periodicity and ratio.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Possible DNS Tunneling Exfiltration with Long Labels and High Volume
rules.description: Detects one client sending many DNS queries whose names carry very long encoded labels. Attackers use this pattern to move stolen data out through DNS.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Large Outbound Flow on Non-Standard Port with No TLS Metadata
rules.description: Detects a very large outbound TCP flow to an uncommon port where the Zeek conn log shows no identified service. Combined with an absence check against TLS logs, this is a strong sign of raw symmetric-encrypted exfiltration.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: SCP or SFTP Client Connecting to a Public IP
rules.description: Detects scp, sftp, pscp, or psftp client processes opening a network connection to a public address. Bulk copies with these tools are a common T1048.002 pattern. Join with Sysmon Event ID 1 (see the matching SPL query) to see the command line that started the transfer.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: FTP STOR Upload to External Server
rules.description: Detects an FTP STOR command, which uploads a file to an FTP server. Data sent this way is in cleartext, so attackers use it to move collected data out of the network.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Archive Staging Followed by Copy to Removable Volume
rules.description: Detects file writes to a removable drive letter within 30 minutes after an archive was created in a user temp folder. This chain is the classic insider exfiltration path over physical medium (ATT&CK T1052 / T1052.001).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Suspicious File Write Burst to a Removable Volume
rules.description: Detects a burst of file-create events on a removable-volume drive letter within five minutes, the signature of an insider bulk copy or an implant packing data onto a stick.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Remote thread created in a trusted Windows process from outside C:\Windows
rules.description: Detects Sysmon EventID 8 where a remote thread is created in a high-value trusted process (svchost, explorer, lsass, winlogon) by a process outside C:\Windows. Matches T1055-style injection used by C2 implants. ATT&CK v20 renamed tactic TA0005 from Defense Evasion to Stealth; the Sigma tactic tag attack.defense_evasion keeps the older tag name.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: DLL Injection Remote Thread at LoadLibrary
rules.description: Detects Sysmon event ID 8 where a new remote thread starts in a LoadLibrary family function. This is the classic final step of dynamic-link library injection (MITRE ATT&CK T1055.001).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Remote Thread Started at Unbacked Address
rules.description: Detects a remote thread whose start address is not backed by any loaded module (Sysmon Event ID 8 with empty StartModule or StartFunction). This is a strong sign of portable executable injection, reflective loading, or shellcode execution.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Cross-Process Handle Access With Memory Write and Thread Context Rights
rules.description: Detects a process opening another process with access rights that permit writing to its memory and manipulating its threads. This is the core primitive of thread execution hijacking, MITRE ATT&CK T1055.003. The thread-context change itself happens on a thread handle (OpenThread with THREAD_SET_CONTEXT 0x0010), which Sysmon Event ID 10 does not log as a separate event. The companion SPL adds a cross-process check (TargetImage != SourceImage) that basic Sigma field matching cannot express.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Early Bird APC Injection - Suspended Child of Script or Office Host
rules.description: Detects the signature Early Bird pattern of T1055.004. A script or Office host creates a process with the CREATE_SUSPENDED flag, which is the usual setup step before QueueUserAPC injection. Note that legit svchost.exe children come from services.exe, so any other parent is already unusual.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Windows Defender Trojan Verdict on Executable in Downloads or Temp
rules.description: Detects Windows Defender malware verdicts whose detection name indicates a trojan family and whose target file is an executable in a user download or temporary directory. Trojanized installers that stage code through TLS callbacks (T1055.005) typically arrive and land exactly this way.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Ptrace Attach to a Long-Running Daemon
rules.description: Detects a ptrace attach request (PTRACE_ATTACH, first argument 0x10) made by a process that is not a known developer or support tool. Attackers use the attach to stop a trusted daemon and inject code into it (MITRE ATT&CK T1055.008).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Linux Proc Memory File Opened With Write Access
rules.description: Detects a process opening /proc/<pid>/mem with write access (O_WRONLY or O_RDWR) and success. On Linux, /proc/<pid>/mem is the procfs view of a process memory. A successful write-flags open by a non-debugger process is the core step of T1055.009 (Proc Memory) injection and is rare in normal operations.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Suspicious Cross-Process Handle Access to a GUI Process with Full Access Rights
rules.description: Detects a non-system process requesting full access rights (for example 0x1F0FFF) to a well-known benign GUI application process. Extra Window Memory Injection (T1055.011) needs cross-process window access before it writes to the extra window memory and swaps the window procedure. Check the call trace and the source process for follow-up.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Suspicious svchost.exe Parent Process
rules.description: Detects svchost.exe starting with a parent that is not a known Windows service host parent. Process hollowing creates svchost.exe from a user-mode loader, so this rule catches the setup step.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Process Creation from Transient Location (Possible Doppelgänging Loader)
rules.description: Detects process creation where the reported image sits in a user-writable or transient folder. During Process Doppelgänging the backing file is rolled back, so the on-disk path stops resolving moments later. Join this event with a file inventory or an EDR existence check to confirm that the image is gone.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Ptrace Attach or Cross-Process Memory Write Targeting a Resident Daemon
rules.description: Detects successful ptrace, process_vm_writev, or process_vm_readv calls that did not come from a known debug tool. VDSO hijacking needs an existing memory-write primitive inside the victim process, and this is how attackers get one. The daemon-target refinement is applied in the SPL via an asset list.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Rare High-Rights ProcessAccess Against Explorer (ListPlanting Write Setup)
rules.description: Flags uncommon processes requesting near-full handle access to explorer.exe. Attackers performing ListPlanting need such a handle before sending LVM window messages or copying code with another Process Injection method.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: PowerShell Download Cradle with Invoke-Expression
rules.description: Detects PowerShell processes combining download methods with expression invocation, typical of download-and-execute cradles used to fetch second-stage payloads.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Proxy Beacon Periodicity to One External Host
rules.description: Detects one internal host that sends many HTTP POST requests to the same external host in a short window, with a stable response size. This is the classic HTTPS C2 beacon pattern used by T1071 operators.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: TFTP Client Network Activity on a Windows Server
rules.description: Detects the built-in Windows TFTP client opening network connections. Servers should not fetch files with TFTP. Intruders use it for fast, unauthenticated tool staging, as in threat THR-01 on this page.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Workstation Opens Direct SMTP Session to External Host
rules.description: Detects a host in the workstation subnet speaking SMTP directly to an external server. Normal mail clients hand messages to the corporate relay, so direct outbound SMTP from user subnets usually means a mail-protocol C2 channel or file exfiltration over SMTP (ATT&CK T1071.003).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: DNS TXT Query Volume Spike from a Single Client
rules.description: One client sends more than 100 TXT queries within 15 minutes. That is the classic shape of DNS tunneling exfiltration, where stolen data rides in the subdomain labels of one external zone.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: MQTT Egress from IoT VLAN to Public Addresses
rules.description: Detects outbound MQTT connections on ports 1883 or 8883 from the IoT VLAN to addresses outside the approved broker list. Publish and subscribe brokers are a known command and control channel for IoT malware such as Muhstik.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Remote Logon by Privileged Account Outside Approved Path
rules.description: Detects a network (type 3) or remote interactive (type 10) logon where the target account is privileged. Privilege is known in two ways: an account name suffix convention (-adm / _admin), or a daily SIEM enrichment lookup that adds IsPrivilegedAccount from group membership. Privileged accounts should log in from jump hosts, not from arbitrary remote sources.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Successful Logon with the Built-in Windows Guest Account
rules.description: Detects a successful logon (Windows Security event 4624) with the built-in Guest account. Guest has no daily-work role and is disabled in hardened images, so any success means untracked local access, or a golden image that silently re-enables the account.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Privileged Domain Account Logon on a Non-DC Host
rules.description: Detects an interactive or remote-interactive logon (types 2, 7, 10) where the target account belongs to a privileged Tier-0 domain group and the receiving host is not a domain controller. Such logons cache high-value credentials on lower-tier hosts and enable domain-wide credential theft.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Built-in Administrator (RID 500) RDP Logon from a User Workstation
rules.description: Detects an RDP (LogonType 10) logon with the built-in Administrator account by SID -500, excluding approved jump hosts by client workstation name. Matching by SID keeps the rule working after the account is renamed.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: AWS Root User Console Login
rules.description: Detects any console sign-in performed by the AWS account root user. Root use should be limited to a documented break-glass procedure, so every login must be reviewed even when it is expected. MFAUsed equal to No raises the urgency further, because it means the root password alone opened the console.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: C2 Beacon to Rented Port-Redirector Proxy Infrastructure
rules.description: Detects allowed egress from a workstation or server to infrastructure that behaves like a rented port-redirector relay (HTRAN, ngrok, FRP, or a plain VPS). The enrichment pipeline provides dest_asn_category and dest_domain. Attackers use such relays to hide the true C2 server from firewall logs.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Netsh Portproxy Forwarding Rule Added on Endpoint or Server
rules.description: Detects creation of a Windows port forwarding rule with 'netsh interface portproxy add'. Attackers use this built-in feature to turn a compromised host into an internal proxy that forwards C2 between network segments (MITRE ATT&CK T1090.001). The rule is stored in the registry and survives reboots.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Outbound C2 Beacon to a Rare Hosting-ASN IP
rules.description: Detects allowed outbound connections from an internal host to an external IP whose enriched ASN type is hosting. Adversaries relay C2 traffic through port redirectors on rented VPS or cloud hosts (T1090.002), so a steady flow to a hosting ASN with no business owner is the core signal. The matching Splunk search adds a volume threshold per source and destination pair.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Tor Client or Pluggable Transport Process Creation
rules.description: Detects the creation of a Tor client process or a Tor pluggable transport helper on a Windows endpoint. Attackers bundle Tor with an implant so that command and control can reach a hidden service over a multi-hop proxy chain. A Tor process on a managed endpoint is a strong signal of covert C2 activity.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: HTTPS Session Where TLS SNI Differs from HTTP Host Header (Domain Fronting)
rules.description: Detects HTTPS sessions where the TLS SNI value differs from the HTTP Host header. This is the core pattern of domain fronting (ATT&CK T1090.004), for example a Cobalt Strike Malleable C2 profile that beacons through a CDN. The rule needs a TLS-inspecting proxy that records both tls_sni and http_host, or a derived boolean sni_host_mismatch that the proxy or the SIEM pipeline computes per session. Zeek alternative: join ssl.log and http.log on uid and compare ssl.server_name with http.host.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Executable File Written to Removable Media on OT-Adjacent Host
rules.description: Detects executable or archive files written to removable media paths on hosts near OT/air-gapped zones. Legitimate transfers only happen at dedicated transfer stations, so any other media write is a policy violation and a possible worm staging event.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Non-Browser Process Connection to Paste Site (T1102)
rules.description: Detects a Windows process that is not a web browser opening an outbound connection to a public paste site. Malware uses paste raw pages as a dead drop resolver (T1102.001) or as a low-profile command channel (parent T1102).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Suspicious Non-Browser Fetch of Paste or Gist Raw Endpoint
rules.description: Detects an HTTP GET to the raw view of a paste or gist endpoint from a client that does not look like a normal browser. Malware abuses these pages as dead drop resolvers (MITRE ATT&CK T1102.001): the page holds an encoded blob that points to the real C2 server.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Regular Polling of Chat Bot API getUpdates Endpoint
rules.description: Detects hosts repeatedly requesting a chat bot API tasking endpoint (getUpdates-style). Regular small polls are the inbound half of bidirectional communication over a web service (MITRE ATT&CK T1102.002).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Repeated Identical GET to Public Content Page with Non-Browser User Agent
rules.description: A single source host repeatedly requests the exact same public content page (video page, social post, RSS item) with a user agent that does not belong to a browser. Malware families such as LURK and PIXSTEAM pulled tasking from video comment sections this way (T1102.003).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Base64-Looking URI Parameter to Non-Approved Destination
rules.description: Detects long Base64-shaped values in HTTP URI parameters where the destination is not on the internal allow-list. Matches implant task retrieval over HTTP, the textbook T1132.001 pattern (threat TH-01).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Base64 String in URL Query Parameter (C2 Tasking)
rules.description: Detects long Base64-shaped values in URL query parameters. Implants commonly carry command-and-control tasking this way (MITRE ATT&CK T1132.001).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Periodic Same-Size HTTP Posts with High-Entropy Bodies (XOR C2 Beacon)
rules.description: Detects a host that repeats HTTP posts of near-constant size to one destination at fixed intervals. Rolling-key XOR beacons produce this shape because the encoded body has high entropy and no padding.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Path Traversal Token on Remote Access Gateway
rules.description: Detects path traversal tokens on authentication or API paths of remote access gateways. Matches pre-auth exploitation patterns such as Ivanti CVE-2023-46805 against external remote services.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Many Special-Privilege Logons for One Account in 10 Minutes
rules.description: An account collecting special privileges on many hosts in a short window often means stolen-token movement between systems. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: NewCredentials Logon (Type 9) with runas
rules.description: Logon type 9 means Windows received new credentials for the session. The normal source is runas /netonly, which attackers also abuse to act under another identity without a new interactive logon.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Process from a User Folder Opens LSASS
rules.description: On a home PC, almost no legitimate program in a user-writable folder has a reason to open LSASS. Every hit deserves a check.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: SeDebugPrivilege Enabled Through a Token Right Adjustment
rules.description: Event 4700 records a token right adjustment. SeDebugPrivilege allows opening protected processes, which credential and token theft tools need.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Service Account Signs In from Two Countries in One Hour
rules.description: A stolen cloud token is often replayed from another country or a hosting service. Watch for one account with successful sign-ins from more than one country in a short window. Field names follow the Microsoft Entra sign-in schema; adjust them to your table. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Suspicious Read Access to LSASS Memory
rules.description: A process opens lsass.exe with access rights that allow reading its memory. Tools that dump credentials or steal tokens need this first.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: SYSTEM Script Host Spawned by the Service Manager
rules.description: services.exe starting cmd, PowerShell, or script hosts as SYSTEM is a common pattern in service and token abuse chains. Known management agents must be filtered.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Token Impersonation Tooling on the Command Line
rules.description: Well-known red-team and admin tooling for stealing or making Windows access tokens appears in a process command line.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Browser Process Spawning Script Interpreter
rules.description: Detects a web browser spawning command-line interpreters or script hosts. This relationship appears when drive-by exploits hand off to a payload, regardless of which vulnerability was used.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: SQL Injection Pattern in Web Request
rules.description: Detects common SQL injection control tokens in web request URIs. Mass scanners and targeted exploitation both leave these patterns in access logs.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: GitHub Branch Protection Rule Deleted
rules.description: A branch protection rule was removed. Attackers preparing to poison a build often delete protection before pushing unreviewed code to a release branch. This also covers insider mistakes that weaken review.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: GitHub Webhook Created to Non-Approved Host
rules.description: Webhooks push repository events, including source code metadata, to external services. Attackers with forge access use them for quiet exfiltration. Only approved integration hosts should ever appear.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Vendor Business Layer Host Spawning Shell or Script Host
rules.description: Detects a fleet-deployed vendor business layer service starting command shells, scripting hosts, or certificate utilities. This is the SolarWinds SUNBURST pattern: a trusted, signed service process acting as the parent of attacker commands.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: BMC Management Interface Reached from Non-Management Subnet
rules.description: Server management controllers (BMCs) must be reachable only from the dedicated management subnets. Any other source reaching them means a segmentation failure that puts server firmware within reach.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: RMM Agent Spawning Shell or Downloader
rules.description: Detects RMM agent processes (Kaseya, ConnectWise, ScreenConnect and similar) spawning shells or downloaders. When an RMM platform is compromised, mass exploitation flows through exactly this parent-child relationship.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Process Execution Directly from Removable Drive Path
rules.description: Detects processes executed directly from drive-letter paths typical of removable media. With storage device control in place, any such execution is suspicious and often marks an infected USB initial-access attempt.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Secure Delete or Wipe Utility Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of SDelete or cipher with the overwrite flag, the two most common secure-delete tools on Windows. Wipers and careful intruders use them to make deleted data unrecoverable.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Short-Expiry Lifecycle Rule Applied to an S3 Bucket
rules.description: Detects PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration calls that enable object expiration after one day or less. An attacker with the PutLifecycleConfiguration permission can use this to destroy all objects in a bucket on a timer, per MITRE ATT&CK T1485.001.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Ransomware Canary File Modification (Windows)
rules.description: Detects any write to a planted canary file under the Canary folder. Legitimate software never touches these files, so a single event means ransomware or a destructive tool is active on this host and response must start now.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Security Service Stopped via Service Control Manager
rules.description: Detects stop events for security and monitoring services such as Sysmon, Windows Defender and EDR agents, which attackers stop to remove visibility before the main attack.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Shadow Copy Deletion via Vssadmin or WMI
rules.description: Detects deletion of Volume Shadow Copies with vssadmin.exe or wmic.exe, a classic ransomware precursor that removes local restore points before encryption.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: SQL Injection Probes Against Public Web Application (Defacement Pre-Stage)
rules.description: Detects SQL injection syntax in query strings and known injection tool user agents in web server traffic. This is the primary access path that leads to external defacement (threat TH-01).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Out-of-Window UPDATE on Internal Portal Content Tables
rules.description: Detects UPDATE statements against portal content tables from accounts outside the approved release set. Public reporting shows internal dashboard and intranet text is a common internal defacement target (T1491.001).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Webserver SQL Injection Probe or Scripted CMS Admin Access
rules.description: Detects SQL injection probes against CMS query parameters and administrative POST requests made with scripted user agents. This is the dominant entry path (TH-01) that ends in external defacement (T1491.002) after exploitation of a public-facing application.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Firmware Copy, Erase, or Verification Failure on Edge Device
rules.description: Detects image copies to flash, flash erase commands, or firmware verification failures on network edge devices. Matches flash-overwrite behavior such as the VPNFilter kill stage (T1495).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Potential Cryptocurrency Miner Execution
rules.description: Detects process creation where image name, path, or command line matches cryptocurrency miner patterns, including renamed miners started from temp paths by web-server processes. Maps to ATT&CK T1496 / T1496.001 and analytic AN0741.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Cryptocurrency Miner Started by Web Server or From Temp Path
rules.description: Detects Linux process creation where the image name, temp-file path, or command line matches cryptocurrency miner patterns. Covers miners renamed and started by web-server processes, as seen in 8220 Gang and Kinsing campaigns. Maps to ATT&CK T1496.001 and analytic AN1490 of detection strategy DET0540.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Proxy Client Execution from Installer or Temp Path
rules.description: Detects execution of residential proxy client binaries, including the Ngioweb name and the svhost masquerade, and common SOCKS proxy flags. Proxyware is often bundled with cracked software or fake VPN apps. Maps to ATT&CK T1496.002, detection strategy DET0028, analytics AN0080 and AN0081.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: OTP Request Velocity Spike from a Single ASN
rules.description: Detects an hourly OTP aggregate in which one source ASN sends far more requests than the endpoint baseline while almost none of the passcodes are verified. This is the access pattern of SMS pumping (ATT&CK T1496.003) against public signup and verification forms on SaaS platforms.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: AWS SES Send Primitives Used by Unapproved Principal
rules.description: Detects SES sending API calls (SendEmail, SendRawEmail, SendBulkTemplatedEmail) issued by a principal that is not an approved sender role. Mass phishing from a compromised identity is the core pattern of ATT&CK T1496.004. Maps to analytic AN0417 of detection strategy DET0147.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Spike of Denied Firewall Sessions Indicates Possible Network Flood
rules.description: Detects an abnormal number of denied or blocked sessions at the network edge within a short window. A network denial of service sends traffic the edge must drop, so a sharp deny-count rise is a strong early indicator for T1498 and its sub-techniques T1498.001 and T1498.002.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: TCP SYN Flood Detected via Zeek Connection Attempt Spike
rules.description: Detects a TCP SYN flood: a very large number of connection attempts that never complete, concentrated on one destination service within one minute. Zeek records these as conn_state S0 (attempt seen, no reply) or REJ (rejected). A scan spreads across ports; a flood concentrates on one.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Inbound Flood of UDP DNS Replies on the Victim Edge
rules.description: Detects a DNS amplification flood from the victim's point of view: thousands of inbound UDP packets with source port 53 arriving within one minute. The victim never sent matching queries, so this reply storm is unsolicited attack traffic generated by abused open resolvers.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Cisco ASA Threat Detection Drop for TCP SYN Flood
rules.description: Detects Cisco ASA threat-detection messages (733100) that report dropped packets because a rate threshold was exceeded, commonly a TCP SYN flood against one exposed host. Matches endpoint resource exhaustion floods.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Linux Kernel Possible SYN Flooding Message
rules.description: Detects the Linux kernel message that appears when the TCP half-open backlog overflows and SYN cookies start. Maps to ATT&CK T1499.001.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Nginx Worker Connection Exhaustion Alert
rules.description: Detects the nginx alert that appears when a worker runs out of connection slots. Slow-header or connection floods hold every socket open until this message appears (MITRE ATT&CK T1499.002).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: PostgreSQL Slow-Query Flood Possible Application Exhaustion
rules.description: Many PostgreSQL statements slower than 10 seconds within a short window, consistent with an expensive-parameter application exhaustion flood (T1499.003).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Repeated Identical Application Crash of the Same Module (Windows Event ID 1000)
rules.description: Detects three or more Application Error events (Event ID 1000) sharing the same faulting module on one computer within 30 minutes. Repeating identical crash signatures are the fingerprint of exploitation-based denial of service (T1499.004): crafted input keeps killing the same process while the watchdog keeps restarting it.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Cloud CLI Token Cache Copied or Archived
rules.description: An archiving, copy, or shell command touches local token caches and secret files of cloud CLIs (Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, SSH). Infostealers and hands-on attackers grab these files to reuse valid tokens (T1528.001).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Non-Browser Process Touches Browser Cookie Store
rules.description: A process that is not a web browser creates or writes to the cookie database of Chrome, Edge, or Firefox. Malware and infostealers do this to copy web session cookies and reuse them on another machine (T1528.004).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Pentest Tool User Agent in AWS Security Token Service Calls
rules.description: AWS STS token calls (AssumeRole, GetSessionToken, GetFederationToken) arrive with a user agent that belongs to attack or scan tools. This often means someone is replaying or testing stolen AWS credentials or tokens (T1528.001).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Stolen Okta Session - Same User From Several IP Addresses
rules.description: One Okta user completes SSO from more than one IP address inside a short time window. This can mean that a session token was stolen and replayed from another machine (T1528.004). Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Successful Device Code Sign-In From Unusual Country
rules.description: A sign-in completed with the device code flow from a country your users do not use. Attackers phish employees into entering a device code so that the attacker receives a valid OAuth token (T1528.003).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Possible Stolen Refresh Token - Non-Interactive Sign-In From New Country
rules.description: A non-interactive sign-in (refresh token or cached token) succeeded from a country that your users do not normally use, with no second factor. This is a common pattern when an attacker replays a stolen token.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Golden SAML Preparation - ADFS Certificate Dump or Export Tools
rules.description: Someone runs known tools or commands used to read or export the AD FS token-signing certificate and its keys. With this certificate an attacker can forge SAML tokens for any user (T1528.002, Golden SAML).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Risky OAuth Application Consent Grant
rules.description: A user consented to an OAuth application that asks for risky mail or file permissions. Consent phishing gives the attacker a valid token without a password. Covers MITRE ATT&CK T1528.003 (OAuth Token).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Forced Shutdown or Reboot of Servers via Command Line
rules.description: Detects forced shutdown and restart commands on servers using shutdown.exe, PowerShell, or wmic. Destructive malware such as APT37 tools and Black Basta use these commands to drop sessions and trigger boot-level payloads.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Bulk Domain Account Deletion or Disablement on a Domain Controller
rules.description: Detects bursts of account deletions (Event 4726) or disables (Event 4725) on domain controllers within ten minutes. Bulk removal by one subject matches documented ransomware behavior such as Akira, which deletes admin accounts before encryption.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Raw Disk Access to PhysicalDrive by Unknown Process
rules.description: Detects Sysmon RawAccessRead events where a process opens a physical drive device path such as \\.\PhysicalDrive0, which destructive tools use to reach and corrupt boot records and file system structures.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Mass File Overwrite Burst by Single Unsigned Process
rules.description: Detects a single process creating or overwriting an extreme number of files within five minutes on a Windows host, the dominant pattern of a disk content wipe (MITRE ATT&CK T1561.001).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Raw Physical Drive Access from Untrusted Path
rules.description: Detects any process opening a raw physical disk device, the signature move of structure-wipe malware such as NotPetya. Excludes software installed under Program Files (backup and imaging tools).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Suspicious UPDATE on High-Value Database Tables
rules.description: Detects UPDATE statements that change balance, amount, or status columns on business tables from a user that is not on the approved writer list. This matches fraudulent transaction injection and stored record manipulation, including behavior reported for FIN13 and Elephant Beetle.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Suspicious UPDATE on Balance or Amount Columns in MySQL
rules.description: Detects UPDATE, DELETE, or TRUNCATE statements that touch balance, amount, or status columns of finance tables, run by a user that is not an application service account. Direct database edits are the core move of stored data manipulation (T1565.001).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Windows TCP/IP Address Conflict Detected (Event 4199)
rules.description: Detects Microsoft-Windows-Tcpip Event ID 4199. The system logs this event when another device on the local network claims the same IP address. An attacker claiming the victim IP or the gateway IP with a second MAC is positioning for on-path traffic interception.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Remote Thread Created in Business Application Process
rules.description: Detects Sysmon EventID 8 (CreateRemoteThread) into business-critical application processes such as finance, ERP, or reporting tools. Attackers inject code to patch in-memory data and change what the application displays or produces (MITRE ATT&CK T1565.003).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Delivered Inbound Reply-Style Message (Hunt for Unknown Sender Domains)
rules.description: Detects inbound delivered mail whose subject starts with RE: or FW: for analyst review. The rule itself does not check the sender, so join it with your partner-domain list to surface messages whose sender domain is not a known partner. Thread hijacking hides phishing links inside real conversations; the subject style and the new domain together break the illusion.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: High Volume Inbound SMTP Connection Wave from One Source
rules.description: Detects a burst of inbound SMTP connections from a single source within five minutes on a Postfix relay. Malspam campaigns produce this pattern before any filter learns the campaign. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Mobile Device Opens Parcel or Pickup Themed Link
rules.description: Detects a corporate device fetching a parcel, pickup, or delivery themed page from a mobile browser. Smishing campaigns use these exact words to move staff off email and onto phones.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Mobile User Agent Reaches Look-Alike Login Page
rules.description: Detects a mobile browser opening a login-shaped page on a host that mimics Microsoft-style sign-in naming but is not Microsoft. QR-code phishing pushes victims to exactly this flow on their phones.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Office Application Spawning Command Interpreter
rules.description: Detects Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or Outlook starting powershell, cmd, mshta, or the Windows Script Host. This is the classic macro phishing execution pattern (T1566.001 followed by user execution).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Office or Mail Client Writes Disk Image or Script Container
rules.description: Detects Outlook or Office applications creating ISO, IMG, LNK, HTA, or CHM files on disk. Attackers wrap payloads in these containers to slip past macro blocks; a mail client has no reason to produce them.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Okta MFA Factor Reset or Deactivation
rules.description: Detects a successful reset or deactivation of a multi-factor factor in Okta. Vishing attackers call the help desk, ask for this reset, and enroll their own device minutes later. Join with the following enrollment event for high confidence.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Remote Access Tool Started from a User-Writable Folder
rules.description: Detects AnyDesk, TeamViewer, ScreenConnect, RemoteUtilities, or Atera starting from Temp, Downloads, or AppData. Callback phishing operators talk victims into running these tools; managed deployments come from Program Files.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Successful High-Risk Sign-In (Password Replay Pattern)
rules.description: Detects a successful sign-in that Microsoft Entra ID scored as high risk. Credential replay from a phishing kit or an anonymizing network usually arrives as a password-only, single-factor sign-in from a new network; enrich the alert by checking authenticationDetails for a lone Password entry and authenticationRequirement for singleFactorAuthentication.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: User Consents to OAuth Application with Mail Scope
rules.description: Detects a user-level OAuth consent grant in the Microsoft 365 Unified Audit Log. Consent phishing needs exactly this event; scopes with Mail.Read and offline_access hand the attacker a lasting token.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Email Delivered with a Risky Attachment File Type
rules.description: Detects inbound email carrying historically abused attachment types (disk images, macro documents, OneNote, shortcuts). Field names follow Defender for Office 365 (EmailAttachmentInfo): FileName, DeliveryAction, SenderAddress, RecipientAddress, Subject. For other gateways (Proofpoint, Mimecast, Barracuda), map these five fields once in your ingest pipeline.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Microsoft Office for macOS Spawned a Script Interpreter or Download Tool
rules.description: Detects Microsoft Office applications on macOS starting shells, scripting tools, or downloaders - the macOS version of macro payload execution after a phishing attachment (T1566.001).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: MS Office Application Spawned a Script or Shell Interpreter
rules.description: Detects a Microsoft Office application starting a command line or script interpreter. Strong sign that a macro or exploit inside an email attachment (T1566.001) is executing attacker code.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Office-Descendant Process Created Run Key or Startup Persistence
rules.description: Detects Office applications or PowerShell writing to autostart registry locations. Malware from a phishing attachment (T1566.001) survives reboots this way (T1547.001).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Office or PowerShell Process Opened an External Network Connection
rules.description: Detects Office applications or PowerShell initiating outbound network connections to non-private addresses. Payload download (T1105) and C2 beaconing (T1071.001) after a spearphishing attachment (T1566.001) both look like this.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Office Process Dropped an Executable or Script into a Temp Folder
rules.description: Detects Microsoft Office applications writing executable or script files into user-writable temp directories - payload staging after a malicious attachment (T1566.001).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: One Sender Domain Sent Attachments to Many Users
rules.description: Trend rule for mass attachment campaigns (precursor to T1566.001). Uses Sigma aggregation: count inbound mails with attachments per sender domain and alert above a threshold. The SenderDomain field must exist in your logs (most gateways add it; in Splunk we derive it from SenderAddress with eval - see the SPL below). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(SenderDomain) > 20 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Suspicious Child Process Spawned by Outlook or Office
rules.description: Detects Office and Outlook applications spawning script or shell child processes, a common follow-up behavior after a user opens a malicious spearphishing attachment.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: PowerShell Download Cradle or Encoded Execution in Command Line
rules.description: Detects PowerShell fetching and running remote content, or certutil used as a downloader. Common second stage after a malicious email attachment (T1566.001).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Suspicious Process Execution from a Linux Mail or Temp Directory
rules.description: Implements the Linux part of the official ATT&CK analytic AN0656: links email delivery to later process execution from mail directories. Works with Sysmon for Linux, osquery process_events, or any Linux EDR that fills the process_creation fields.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Windows Defender Detected Malware After an Email Attachment
rules.description: Aggregates Microsoft Defender malware detection events. Blocked is not safe: campaigns retry with new variants, so every detection after a phishing wave (T1566.001) needs human review.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Browser Access to Newly Registered Domain Serving a Login Page (Possible AiTM)
rules.description: Detects browser sessions to domains registered in the last 14 days that serve login-style paths. Attackers register fresh domains for credential phishing pages that proxy real SSO portals (adversary-in-the-middle).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Office Application Spawning a Script Interpreter
rules.description: Detects Microsoft Office processes acting as the parent of script or shell interpreters. This is the classic post-download execution pattern for documents delivered through legitimate file-sharing services.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Remote Access Tool Service Installed (Windows Event 7045)
rules.description: Detects installation of a Windows service for remote access software. Service installation makes the attacker's tool survive reboots and is a strong persistence signal in vishing incidents.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Consumer Cloud Storage Upload with Sync Tool User Agent
rules.description: Detects uploads to consumer cloud storage with sync-tool user agents such as rclone, azcopy, or MEGAync, or direct uploads to known personal storage endpoints. This is the dominant pre-encryption exfiltration pattern in modern ransomware playbooks.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Git Push to a Non-Corporate Remote
rules.description: Detects a git client pushing to a remote that is not on the corporate allow-list. Intruders with a stolen developer session commonly add their own remote and run git push --all and git push --tags to move the whole repository out in one step.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Rclone Command-Line Tool Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of rclone, the tool most commonly abused for bulk exfiltration to cloud storage services such as Mega, Google Drive or attacker-owned S3 buckets. rclone activity on servers hours before ransomware encryption is a known pre-encryption pattern (see ATT&CK C0015 and leaked ransomware playbooks).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Egress POST to Text Storage Sites from Server Subnets
rules.description: Detects HTTP POST requests to well-known paste and text storage domains from addresses classified as servers or infrastructure. A server that posts to a paste site is a strong T1567.003 exfiltration signal regardless of request size.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Suspicious Discord Webhook URL in Process Command Line
rules.description: Detects process creations whose command line references a Discord webhook URL, a common exfiltration channel for info stealers and loaders.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: High NXDOMAIN burst from one client
rules.description: Detects a client that receives many NXDOMAIN answers for random-looking external names within five minutes. This fits a domain generation algorithm trying many candidate C2 names, for example ransomware searching for a live failover channel.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: DNS Name Resolved to Many Distinct IPs in One Hour (Fast Flux)
rules.description: Detects a single DNS name that returned more than 20 different IP addresses within one hour. Fast flux domains rotate A records very fast so that one name always points to a live relay. Content delivery networks behave in a similar way, so keep an allow list of known CDN names and network owners.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: High NXDOMAIN Burst from a Single Host
rules.description: One host asks many different domain names in five minutes and most answers are NXDOMAIN. Malware with a domain generation algorithm does this while it walks its candidate list looking for the one name the attacker registered today.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Windows Process Connects on a High Port to a Fresh DNS Answer IP
rules.description: Detects a Windows process opening an outbound TCP connection to a high, non-standard destination port. This is the per-event precursor for DNS Calculation (T1568.003): the full detection joins Sysmon Event ID 22 (DNS query) with Event ID 3 (network connection) on ProcessGuid and tests whether the connection port equals a calculation on the answer octets, exactly as the matching SPL below implements per the official analytic AN0728.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: TLS Connection with Self-Signed or Untrusted Certificate
rules.description: Detects outbound TLS connections where Zeek records a self-signed or otherwise untrusted server certificate. Attack tooling often generates its own certificates, while enterprise clients normally terminate on certificates from a public or internal certificate authority. Excludes RFC1918 destinations.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Network Session with Unidentified Service on TLS-Like Port
rules.description: Detects TCP sessions to ports that normally speak TLS where the network sensor could not identify any application protocol. Symmetric-key command and control channels (T1573.001) often use a custom framing protocol with no TLS handshake, so the service field stays empty. Requires Zeek conn logging or an equivalent sensor.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Outbound TLS Session with Self-Signed Server Certificate
rules.description: Detects outbound TLS handshakes where the presented server certificate fails validation because it is self-signed. Attacker-run command and control servers often use their own public-key infrastructure, so a self-signed certificate on an internal client is a strong early signal for T1573.002.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Sinkholed Domain Resolves Again on New Nameservers
rules.description: A domain on the team sinkhole watchlist answers successfully again, usually on new nameservers and new IPs. Fast-flux operators re-delegate blocked domains (T1583.002) within days. Keep the watchlist fed from your own block actions and from intel reports.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Inbound Email from VPS ASN with Failed SPF
rules.description: Detects inbound messages whose sending IP belongs to a hosting ASN and whose SPF validation failed. Attackers host phishing pages (MITRE ATT&CK T1583.003) on rented VPS machines and send matching lures from the same box. Correlate the sender IP with proxy visits in the next 24 hours.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Windows Host Connecting to Bulletproof or Dedicated-Hosting ASN
rules.description: Detects an endpoint process opening a network connection whose destination IP belongs to an ASN classified as bulletproof or dedicated hosting by the intel enrichment pipeline. Such infrastructure is commonly acquired under MITRE ATT&CK T1583.004 to run C2 panels and malware repositories.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Web Server Spawning cmd or PowerShell
rules.description: Looks for a web server worker process (w3wp, httpd, nginx, tomcat) starting cmd, PowerShell, or another script host. This is common after a web shell or upload bug, but some old admin scripts do it too.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Lookalike Domain Lookup on Windows
rules.description: Looks for a Windows DNS query that contains our brand but is not one of the real company domains. Good early warning for lookalike domains used in phishing.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Brand Domain Answer Outside Expected Range
rules.description: Alerts when a partner domain resolves to an address outside the ranges we expect. Could be DNS hijacking, but a CDN or failover change can also explain it.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Endpoint to VPS or Bulletproof IP Range
rules.description: Detects a Windows endpoint connecting to an IP in a known VPS or bulletproof range. These ranges are often used for payload staging or C2.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: POST to Web Shell or Upload Path
rules.description: Looks for a POST to a path that looks like a web shell, upload handler, or command endpoint and gets a 200. A 200 from a catch-all route can still be a false positive, so check the response body if possible.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Nmap or Scanner Running on Windows
rules.description: Detects nmap, masscan, zmap, hping3, or a scanner-like executable running from a temp folder on Windows. Attackers and botnet operators use these to map reachable services.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Service Account Posting to Paste or Code Host
