rules.description: Looks for a service account posting to GitHub, Gist, or Pastebin. Attackers use these services for payload staging and small exfil jobs.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Lambda Change Outside Deployment Pipeline
rules.description: Alerts when a Lambda function is created or changed by a principal outside the deployment pipeline. Could be a break-glass change, so check the ticket.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Network Device Config Change Outside Management
rules.description: Looks for a Cisco config change from outside the management ranges. A console change from a jump host can still be legitimate; verify the source.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Cloud Hosting Domain Access
rules.description: Looks for users opening pages on low-cost cloud hosting domains often used for phishing kits. Check the page before blocking the whole host.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Office Spawning a Script Host
rules.description: Detects Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or OneNote starting PowerShell, cmd, or another script host. This is a common malware delivery chain, but some old templates do it too.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Lookalike Domain on Cheap TLD
rules.description: Looks for DNS queries that contain a brand name and use a cheap TLD the company does not own. Useful for catching lookalike domains before a user clicks.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Server Utility Connecting to Cloud IP
rules.description: Detects built-in Windows utilities connecting to public cloud ranges. These utilities are used for payload download and C2, but also by admins for certificate work.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: New Okta MFA Factor
rules.description: Looks for a new MFA factor being activated in Okta. Account compromise often ends with the attacker adding their own factor.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Risky Social App Sign-In
rules.description: Detects a risky sign-in to a social or code platform that is linked to the corporate identity. Check whether the user was traveling or the session was replayed.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Inbox Rule Hiding Security Mail
rules.description: Detects a new inbox rule that targets security, quarantine, spam, or phishing mail. Attackers use this to hide alerts and replies after taking over a mailbox.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: AWS Console Login Without MFA
rules.description: Detects a successful AWS console login without MFA for a normal user. Break-glass accounts are excluded, but they should be reviewed separately.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: New Cheap Domain with Let's Encrypt Cert
rules.description: Looks for a new cheap domain using a free Let's Encrypt certificate. This is normal for small sites, but also common for short-lived attack infrastructure.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Unsigned Executable from User Folder
rules.description: Detects an unsigned executable running from Temp, Public, or Downloads. Malware often starts this way, but installers and portable apps can also match.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Code Signing Cert Outside PKI
rules.description: Detects a code-signing certificate issued to someone outside the PKI or release groups. Check the request ticket before revoking anything.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Self-Signed TLS on Outbound
rules.description: Detects an outbound TLS connection using a simple self-signed certificate. Some internal tools do this, so check the destination before blocking.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Exploit Tooling Outside Build Host
rules.description: Looks for exploit-development tools on a normal workstation. Build and lab hosts are filtered, but check whether the user is a security engineer.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Executable Staged in User-Writable Path by Browser or Mail Client
rules.description: Detects executable files written by browser, mail, or archive processes into user-writable paths. This is the typical landing pattern of purchased malware and tools obtained through resource development (MITRE ATT&CK T1588, T1588.001, T1588.002).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Known Malware Hash or Family Trait Executes on Windows Host
rules.description: Detects process creation where the file hash is on a threat-intelligence list of known malware samples, or the process image carries a known family filename trait. This is the endpoint echo of malware bought, stolen, or downloaded through resource development (MITRE ATT&CK T1588.001). The two hashes below are synthetic examples; replace them with your TI feed values and keep the rule and the SPL list in sync.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Cobalt Strike Default Named Pipes or Beacon File Names
rules.description: Detects the default named pipes and default executable file names of Cobalt Strike beacons. Cracked or trial builds of the commercial framework often keep these defaults, so the rule also catches tooling obtained through resource development (MITRE ATT&CK T1588, T1588.002).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Validly Signed Driver or Image Loaded from Unexpected Publisher
rules.description: Detects kernel driver loads (Sysmon event 6) and DLL or executable image loads (Sysmon event 7) whose signature status is valid but whose signer is not on a short list of expected publishers. Stolen or abused code signing certificates (MITRE ATT&CK T1588.003) produce exactly this pattern, and CodeIntegrity events 3076 and 3077 record the same anomaly on hosts with application control policy.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Proxy Traffic to Brand Lookalike Domain from CT Enrichment
rules.description: Detects web traffic to a domain whose certificate transparency record matches a brand keyword and whose registration is fresh. The enriched fields brand_hit and domain_age_days come from a CT pipeline that joins the CT stream with registration data (MITRE ATT&CK T1588.004).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Exploit Kit or Known Exploit Payload Detected by Network IDS
rules.description: Detects intrusion detection alerts whose rule names indicate exploit kit activity or known exploit payloads, including leaked exploit tooling. Buying, stealing, or downloading exploits is MITRE ATT&CK T1588.005, and this alert is the direct view of such code in use.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: AWS IAM User or Access Key Creation from Unfamiliar Network
rules.description: Detects IAM CreateUser, CreateAccessKey, or AttachUserPolicy events from source networks outside known corporate or partner ranges. Attackers who just used an N-day weakness in a cloud-edge service often add persistence within minutes (MITRE ATT&CK T1588.006 with T1136).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: AWS AI Model Invocation or Key Creation Outside Corporate Ranges
rules.description: Detects Amazon Bedrock model invocations and new IAM access key creation that originate from infrastructure outside corporate ranges. Anomalous AI API usage, fresh API keys, and dormant identities suddenly calling models are the cloud-side footprint of obtaining access to generative AI tools (MITRE ATT&CK T1588.007).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Risky Cloud Sign-In Success
rules.description: Detects a successful Azure sign-in with medium or high risk. This is not proof of compromise; it just means the identity engine saw something unusual.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Sign-In from Anonymizer or New Risky Device
rules.description: Looks for a successful sign-in from an anonymizer or a new risky device. Useful after credential leaks or phishing-for-information campaigns.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: External Mail Using Internal Display Name
rules.description: Detects external mail using the display name of a known employee. Attackers collect names during recon and reuse them in phishing.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: External Mail Using Staff or Help Desk Name
rules.description: Looks for external mail using a staff or help desk display name. This is a common pretext after employee-name reconnaissance.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Banner Grab Burst on Service Ports
rules.description: One external source opens many short TCP connections to service ports, transfers zero bytes, and ends each one with a reset. This is the typical shape of banner grabbing and service fingerprinting before an attack (MITRE ATT&CK T1590). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(id.orig_h) > 40 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: DNS Probing of Infrastructure Subdomains
rules.description: One external source asks the public DNS server for many infrastructure subdomains such as vpn, mail, owa, and autodiscover in a short time. This is a classic sign of DNS-based network reconnaissance (MITRE ATT&CK T1590). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) > 20 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: External Port Scan Burst Against Public Range
rules.description: Many blocked inbound connections to public-facing hosts from one external source in a short window. This pattern often appears during pre-attack network reconnaissance, when an intruder maps open services before an intrusion (MITRE ATT&CK T1590). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) > 30 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Recon Burst from Hosting or VPN Provider Ranges
rules.description: Denied inbound traffic from source addresses inside known hosting or VPN provider ranges, counted per source in a short window. Attackers rent such exits so their sources look like normal users (MITRE ATT&CK T1590). Replace the placeholder documentation ranges in selection_range with the ranges from your enriched threat feed. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) > 10 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Single Source Probing Many Paths on OWA or Admin Portals
rules.description: One external source requests many different paths under mail and admin portals such as /owa, /ecp, /autodiscover, and /admin in a short window. This path walk often precedes exploitation of public-facing servers (MITRE ATT&CK T1590). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(c-ip) > 20 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: DNS NXDOMAIN Burst from One Source
rules.description: Counts NXDOMAIN answers per external source in a five-minute window on Zeek dns.log data. A wave of misses from one address is the classic shape of a wordlist enumeration run. This covers threat 5 of section 5.3, bulk mapping. Tune the threshold of 40 to sit just above your measured normal noise. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(id.orig_h) > 40 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: DNS Wordlist and Canary Subdomain Probing
rules.description: Detects a source asking for common service names such as vpn, mail, staging or test under the victim domain, or any query for the canary subdomain. This covers threat 2 of section 5.3, hidden portal discovery. A canary hit alone is a strong recon signal with almost no noise. Adjust the name list to your zone. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) > 10 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: DNS Zone Transfer Attempt
rules.description: Detects AXFR zone transfer attempts in name server logs. An outside AXFR asks for a copy of the whole zone in one request, which is reconnaissance of the full record set. This covers threat 3 of section 5.3. Allowlist approved secondaries by address before enabling alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Lookalike Domain Resolution Inside the Network
rules.description: Detects Sysmon Event ID 22 DNS queries where the requested name matches known lookalike patterns for the brand. A resolution from inside the network often means a phishing click on a lookalike domain. This covers threat 1 of section 5.3. Update the pattern list from brand monitoring.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Office 365 Tenant Enumeration via Autodiscover or GetUserRealm
rules.description: Detects one external client sending several requests to autodiscover or GetUserRealm paths on mail-facing web servers. Public API endpoints can confirm cloud use and reveal tenant names without any login. This covers threat 4 of section 5.3. Tune the threshold after a week of baseline data. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(client_ip) > 5 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: DNS Zone Transfer (AXFR) Attempt
rules.description: Detects attempts to perform a DNS zone transfer (AXFR) against an authoritative name server. A successful transfer hands the attacker the full list of records of the zone, so every attempt is worth an alert.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: High-Volume Unique-Query Enumeration of a Zone
rules.description: Detects a single source asking for an unusually high number of unique names under one zone in a short window. This is the pattern of broad record sweeps that map a zone and its cloud vendors. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) > 100 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Reverse DNS (PTR) Sweep
rules.description: Detects a single source issuing many PTR queries in a short window. Walking PTR records across an address block maps server names without touching any system directly. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(id.orig_h) > 30 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Sensitive Subdomain Name Probing
rules.description: Detects a single external source probing several short, sensitive names such as vpn., mail., citrix., jira., or staging. under the victim zone. The attacker is building a list of remote access doors. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(id.orig_h) > 15 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Subdomain Brute Force (NXDOMAIN Storm)
rules.description: Detects a single source receiving many NXDOMAIN answers for names under one zone in a short window. Attackers brute forcing subdomains produce exactly this pattern, because most guessed names do not exist. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(id.orig_h) > 60 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Activity Spike for Guest or External Accounts
rules.description: Detects many network logons (type 3) for one external, guest, or vendor account within one hour. A burst can mean an attacker is walking the trust path with a shared account. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(TargetUserName) > 15 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Cloud SSO Sign-In from External Identity in a New Country
rules.description: Detects a successful cloud SSO sign-in for an external vendor identity from a country that is not on the approved list, often from a new device. Vendor support accounts should sign in only from known places.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Remote Management Tool Connection from a Server Segment
rules.description: Detects a server in the data center range talking to a remote monitoring and management (RMM) service such as AnyDesk, TeamViewer, RustDesk, or Splashtop. Intrusion groups abuse these trusted admin tools after mapping vendor trust.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Repeated Calls to a Vendor Update Endpoint from an Unexpected Server
rules.description: Detects many HTTP calls to a vendor update path from one source in a short window. A trusted update channel that repeats on a fixed schedule can hide a beacon from a trojanized update. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) > 12 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Vendor or Service VPN Login from Unlisted Source IP
rules.description: Detects a vendor or service account logging in to the VPN or firewall from a source IP outside the approved vendor egress pool. This is the classic sign that a trust dependency credential was stolen and is being used.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Edge and VPN Portal Probing
rules.description: Detects one source requesting many VPN, webmail, or admin portal paths on public web servers within ten minutes. This is how an attacker profiles a discovered portal before trying credentials against it. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(clientip) > 20 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Horizontal Sweep Across External Range
rules.description: Detects a single external source denied on many different destination IPs at the firewall boundary in a short window. This is the classic echo of topology mapping before an intrusion. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Internal Mapping with Built-in Windows Tools
rules.description: Detects bursts of nltest, net view, and nbtstat launches on Windows servers. These commands map domains, shares, and NetBIOS names from inside. This is the post-compromise mapping stage, which MITRE tracks under the Discovery tactic. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(User) > 3 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Traceroute Sweep Through UDP High Ports
rules.description: Detects bursts of UDP probes from one external source to the classic traceroute ports (33434 and above). Zeek logs the probes as short connections with no service. Extend the port list if your sensors see other traceroute styles, such as ICMP-based probes. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(id.orig_h) > 10 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Vertical Scan on Single Host
rules.description: Detects one external source denied on many ports of one destination host. This shows the attacker profiling a specific system, often the VPN gateway or a DMZ host. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Banner Grabbing Pattern on Management Services
rules.description: Detects many short connections that open a management port, receive a small answer and close at once (Zeek connection state RSTO). This is how attackers grab banners from services they found in the range (MITRE ATT&CK T1590.005). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(id.orig_h) > 10 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Direct-IP Access Bypassing DNS on Public Web Server
rules.description: Detects web requests where the Host header holds a raw IP address instead of a domain name. This shows that a client found the server address and connected directly, skipping DNS and any CDN protection (MITRE ATT&CK T1590.005). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(client_ip) > 10 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: One External Source Sweeping Many Victim Addresses
rules.description: Detects one external source contacting more than 15 distinct destination IP addresses within five minutes in the connection states S0 or REJ. Wide sweeps of a whole address block are a classic preparation step before active scanning and initial access (MITRE ATT&CK T1590.005). Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: PTR Reverse Sweep Against the Victim Network
rules.description: Detects a burst of reverse DNS (PTR) lookups for addresses inside the victim in-addr.arpa zone. Attackers sweep PTR records to map address blocks to hostnames while staying quiet (MITRE ATT&CK T1590.005). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) > 20 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Remote Access and Management Port Probe Burst
rules.description: Detects one external source sending many denied probes to remote access and management ports such as SSH (22), VPN (1194) and RDP (3389). Attackers use this to find remote access doors inside a scanned range (MITRE ATT&CK T1590.005). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) > 20 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Known-CVE Path Probing on VPN Appliance
rules.description: Detects requests for URI paths tied to published edge appliance CVEs, such as path traversal tricks that leak credentials (T1590.006).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Management Port Sweep across Edge Appliances
rules.description: Detects one source touching management ports (22, 23, 443, 8443) on several edge appliances in a short window (T1590.006).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Repeated TLS Handshakes without Application Data
rules.description: Detects one source opening many TLS sessions to edge appliances with almost no payload, typical for banner and version probing (T1590.006). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(id.orig_h) > 20 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: VPN Admin Portal Probing from One External Source
rules.description: Detects one external source requesting many known VPN admin portal paths in a short window, a classic appliance fingerprinting step (T1590.006). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(client_ip) > 10 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: VPN Portal Credential Stuffing Burst
rules.description: Detects many failed VPN logins from one source in a short window, the follow-up step after leaked or guessed appliance credentials (T1590.006). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) > 5 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: New Sender Domain with Company Pretext
rules.description: Flags mail from a domain registered less than 30 days ago that uses a company or job pretext. Check the domain age source before trusting the alert.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Inbound Mail About Sites or Facilities
rules.description: Looks for inbound mail that talks about sites, depots, warehouses, or gate passes, or comes from a site-themed domain. Site details are useful for physical targeting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Partner Lookalike Sending Payment Mail
rules.description: Detects a partner lookalike domain sending invoice or payment mail. Verify with the partner through a known phone number, not the reply-to.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Urgent Payment Change from External Sender
rules.description: Looks for an external payment-change message with urgent wording. Common BEC pattern, but finance teams do get real urgent bank change requests.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: New Recruiter Domain Mailing Staff
rules.description: Flags a first-seen domain sending recruiter mail to staff. Recruiter pretexts are used to learn roles and reporting lines.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Sensitive Path on Public Web Server
rules.description: Looks for a public web server returning 200 or 206 for.env,.git, backup, dump, or admin config paths. Check whether the path is supposed to be public.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Recruiter Email with Attachment
rules.description: Detects a recruiter-themed email with an attachment from outside the known recruiting platforms. Social-media recon often supplies the role and name.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Search Crawler Fetching Sensitive File
rules.description: Flags a search-engine crawler fetching a sensitive file. Indexed secrets and backups are a common open-web finding.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: GitHub Secret Scanning Alert
rules.description: Detects GitHub secret scanning alerts. A secret in a repo is not always live; check whether the key is valid and rotate if needed.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Sensitive Path on Owned Website
rules.description: Detects requests for source, environment, backup, or admin paths on a public website. Check whether the file is supposed to be reachable.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Scanner User-Agent in Web Logs
rules.description: Looks for scanner User-Agents in web logs. It is noisy on purpose; use it for triage and trend, not as a standalone block.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: External RDP Probe
rules.description: Detects an external RDP probe denied by the firewall. A single event is weak; correlate with repeated attempts from the same source.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Log4Shell JNDI String in Request
rules.description: Looks for a Log4Shell JNDI string in a web request. Most internet noise is opportunistic; check whether the target is vulnerable.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Backup or Source Path Returns 200
rules.description: Detects a backup or source path returning 200. Verify the file is not a decoy or a catch-all response.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: External DNS Zone Transfer Attempt
rules.description: Detects an external AXFR or IXFR request. A zone transfer exposes the full DNS zone; approved secondary servers should be excluded.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Outbound WHOIS on TCP 43
rules.description: Looks for outbound WHOIS on TCP 43. WHOIS is normal during enrichment, so this is mainly useful in bulk or from odd hosts.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Shodan or Censys Crawler
rules.description: Detects known scan-database crawlers such as Shodan, Censys, zgrab, or masscan. Public scan data can expose services without direct exploitation.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Lookalike Login Certificate for Brand
rules.description: Looks for a new certificate that contains our brand and an auth word like login, sso, vpn, or mail on a domain we do not own. Check the certificate owner before blocking.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Detailed Phishing Lure for Executive
rules.description: Detects a quarantined message with report-quality target context aimed at an executive, finance director, or HR lead. This is a high-signal but low-volume rule.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Certificate Leaks Internal Naming
rules.description: Alerts when a certificate exposes an internal naming pattern. This could be a lab certificate or a migration; confirm the source.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Org Chart Sent to Personal Mail
rules.description: Detects an org chart, team structure, or onboarding pack sent to a personal mailbox. This is often the answer to a phishing-for-information request.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Job Offer Mail from New External Domain
rules.description: Looks for a clean inbound job-offer email from a domain not on the recruiting allowlist. Most of these are harmless; review the domain and the request.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Questionnaire Attachment from External Sender
rules.description: Detects external mail with a questionnaire, survey, or compliance form attached. The attachment itself may be harmless; the goal is usually to get data or a click.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Shortened Link Click in Mail
rules.description: Looks for a URL Click event on a public shortener. Shorteners are used to hide phishing and tracking pages, but marketing also uses them.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Teams Call with Internal-Looking Caller ID
rules.description: Detects a Teams PSTN call with a caller ID that starts with our number range. Voice phishing often spoofs an internal-looking number.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Archive or Executable Download from Staging-Friendly File Hosts
rules.description: Detects a user downloading archive, executable, or script content from public file-sharing or code-sharing services commonly abused to stage malware (ATT&CK T1608 / T1608.001). Combine with referer context to find search or webmail-driven delivery.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Archive or Executable Download from Consumer File Hosts
rules.description: Detects a user downloading archive, executable, or script content from consumer file-hosting services that are commonly abused to stage malware (ATT&CK T1608.001). Pair with referer context to spot webmail, search, or forum-driven delivery.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Executable or Archive Download from Code-Host Raw or Release Paths by Non-Developer Subnet
rules.description: Detects a host outside the developer subnets downloading executable or archive content from raw or release paths of code-hosting platforms. Attackers stage tools this way for implants to pull later (ATT&CK T1608.002), and such a pull from a server or office host is almost never legitimate.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Mail Link Points to Domain Younger Than 7 Days
rules.description: Detects mail-gateway URL rewrite or click events where the target domain is younger than 7 days according to a newly-observed-domain enrichment lookup. Attackers who install a fresh TLS certificate (ATT&CK T1608.003) almost always deliver the link by mail, so click-time age scoring catches the certificate abuse even when the message text looks clean.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: First-Seen Script Path Served from Upload or Template Directories
rules.description: Detects HTTP requests for script files inside upload or template directories of your own web estate. Attackers staging a drive-by target (T1608.004) drop an obfuscated loader into these folders and every visitor then fetches it. Alert on first-seen paths and on unusual visitor counts per path.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Script Host Executes a File from the Downloads Folder
rules.description: Endpoint half of malicious-link delivery: a browser saves content fetched through a link (often with a shortener referrer) and a Windows script host then executes a file from the user's Downloads or Temp folder. Matches the user-execution step that follows staged payload links (T1204.001).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: ZIP Download from Long-Tail TLD Host Referred by Search Engine
rules.description: Detects the classic SEO poisoning delivery step (ATT&CK T1608.006): an internal user downloads archive content from a host on a cheap long-tail top-level domain while the HTTP referer points at a large search engine. Gootloader-style campaigns end this step in Windows Script Host execution of an obfuscated JavaScript file, so escalate any hit and check the endpoint for follow-on script activity.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: AI Assistant Referrer Fetches Content from Young Domain
rules.description: Detects proxy requests where the referrer is a known AI assistant or AI search host and the destination domain is only a few days old. Public research (Netcraft, Lasso Security) shows poisoned AI citations route users exactly this way, so the referrer-plus-age join is the earliest reliable web signal for T1608.007.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Finance Keyword Inbox Rule Created or Updated
rules.description: Detects creation or update of a mailbox rule that moves or deletes mail containing invoice, payment, bank or wire keywords. Attackers use such rules to hide BEC threads from the mailbox owner.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Browser Receives Executable from Non-Approved Host (Possible Fake Update)
rules.description: Detects a browser session receiving a Windows executable (fake update pattern) from a host that is not on the approved update source list. Upstream content injection delivers malware this way without touching your servers.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Security Info Registration After Email Bombing Surge
rules.description: Detects a user registering security info (an MFA method) in Entra ID. In the T1667 email bombing pattern this event follows a mailbox flood and a fake IT help desk call, so pair this rule with an inbound mail-volume alert. The registration is often the account-takeover moment.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Client Joined Corporate SSID from Unknown BSSID
rules.description: Detects WLAN-AutoConfig connect events (8001) where clients joined the corporate SSID from a BSSID that is not part of the approved access-point inventory - the client-side signature of an evil twin.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Non-Analyst Threat Vendor Access
rules.description: Looks for users outside the intel team reaching threat-intelligence vendor sites. This is not always malicious; check whether the user has a business reason.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Large Upload to Public AI
rules.description: Detects a large upload to a public AI service. This can be normal work, but it can also be sensitive data leaving the company.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Executive Name from New Domain
rules.description: Looks for a first-contact email that uses an executive display name from a new domain. Verify with the executive through a known channel.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Help Desk Lure from New Domain
rules.description: Detects a first-contact email that pretends to be HR, payroll, or IT support from a very new domain. Check the link before the user clicks.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Finance Meeting from External Domain
rules.description: Looks for a finance-themed meeting created by an external organizer. Verify the meeting through a known internal contact before joining.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: AI Agent Identity Reaching Unsanctioned Webhook or Model API
rules.description: Detects proxy traffic from an AI agent or agent service identity to generic webhook collectors or to model-API endpoints that are not on the approved AI egress list. This is the transfer half of AI-enabled exfiltration (T1700). Approved destinations form AuthorizedAIEndpoints, the list of external services an agent may talk to. Keep that list in a lookup and filter it before alerting.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk
